### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the outgoing transitions of A26 went almost exclusively to A27 (about 95 in 100 of the 201 observed outgoing transitions), with rare alternatives to A08 (about 5 transitions), A20 (about 2), and single transitions to A01, A04 and A06. In the later window, A27 still dominates even more strongly (about 97–98 in 100 of 202 outgoing transitions), and the rare alternatives are now A02 (about 2 transitions) and single transitions to A40, A45 and A31. [DIR001]
- The rare alternative targets differ between the windows, but each of them rests on only one to a few observations, so their appearance or disappearance is consistent with sampling noise in rare variants. [DIR001]
- The overall size of the routing difference is very small (cosine dissimilarity of about 0.0005 on a 0–1 scale), even though it exceeds the difference seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled traces. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The only qualifying item concerns rare alternative transitions out of A26 that are observed one to five times each, while the dominant transition to A27 is essentially unchanged (about 95 in 100 versus about 98 in 100); one item against roughly 0.44 expected by chance across 89 tested units is what an unchanged process typically produces, and the high empirical strength of a single, very small difference cannot rule out a rare-variant sampling effect.

message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

We have one evidence item: DIR001, a control-flow direction indicator for activity A26. It shows the outgoing transition distribution from A26 in the before window vs after window.

Before window (200 traces): A26's outgoing transitions were dominated by A27 (about 95%), with small shares to A08 (about 2.5%), A20 (about 1%), and A01, A04, A06 (each about 0.5%).

After window (200 traces): A27 dominates even more (about 97.5%), with small shares to A02 (about 1%), and A40, A45, A31 (each about 0.5%).

The observed_change is 0.000528 on cosine dissimilarity scale — that's tiny. The empirical_strength is 0.995, meaning 99.5% of reference comparisons had a smaller difference — so this difference is unusual for random splits. But the actual magnitude is minuscule: the distribution is essentially "A26 goes to A27 about 95 in 100 cases before, about 97-98 in 100 cases after". The changes are in rare transitions: A08 dropped from ~2.5% to 0 (not observed), A20 from ~1% to 0, A01/A04/A06 from ~0.5% to 0; new rare transitions A02 (~1%), A40/A45/A31 (~0.5% each) appeared.

Support: 201 outgoing transitions before, 202 after — so roughly 2 outgoing transitions per trace containing A26 (support is outgoing transitions of the source activity). Actually support before 201, after 202 — these are the number of outgoing transitions observed. With ~200 traces, A26 appears in most traces and has about 1 outgoing transition each? Wait, 201 outgoing transitions across 200 traces means A26 appears in most traces with about one outgoing transition each. Hmm, but the shares: A27 at 0.95 of 201 ≈ 191 transitions. A08 at 0.0249 of 201 ≈ 5 transitions. A01, A04, A06 at 0.004975 of 201 ≈ 1 each. A20 at 0.00995 ≈ 2.

After: A27 at 0.975 of 202 ≈ 197. A02 at 0.0099 of 202 ≈ 2. A40, A45, A31 at 0.00495 of 202 ≈ 1 each.

So the rare transitions involve 1-5 observations each. These are exactly the kind of rare-variant fluctuations the guidelines warn about. The main transition A27 stays dominant in both windows (95% → 97.5%).

Screening: 89 units tested, 0.44 items expected without change. We have 1 item. Per the instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

1 item vs 0.44 expected — that's the same order of magnitude (one or two items when fewer than one is expected). So the verdict must be "Insufficient evidence".

Also, the observed change itself is tiny (0.00053 cosine dissimilarity), and the differences are in transitions observed only 1-5 times. The high empirical_strength (0.995) is noted but cannot by itself establish a change.

So:

### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A26's outgoing transitions went almost exclusively to A27 (about 95 in 100 outgoing transitions), with rare transitions to A08 (about 5 of 201 transitions), A20 (about 2), and single occurrences to A01, A04, A06. In the later window, A27 still dominates (about 97-98 in 100), with rare transitions to A02 (about 2 of 202) and single occurrences to A40, A45, A31. The rare alternative targets differ between windows, but each involves only one or a few observations. [DIR001]

- The overall size of the routing difference is very small (cosine dissimilarity about 0.0005), though it is larger than in nearly all random re-splits (about 995 of 1000 reference comparisons). [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The only qualifying item concerns rare alternative transitions from A26 (one to five observations each), while the dominant transition to A27 is essentially unchanged (about 95% vs 98%); one item against an expectation of 0.44 items by chance is what an unchanged process typically produces, and the high empirical strength of a single tiny difference cannot rule out rare-variant sampling.

Let me make sure I follow the format rules:

- Every bullet/paragraph stating a fact about data or hypothesis must end with exactly one pair of square brackets with evidence IDs. So [DIR001] at the end of each bullet.
- First line of Inference: exactly "Support level: Insufficient evidence".
- Then "The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process." plus one short sentence on limitation.

Let me write the observed differences carefully with rounded percentages or fractions.

Before: A27 95.0%, A08 2.5%, A20 1.0%, A01/A04/A06 0.5% each. Out of 201 outgoing transitions: A27 ≈ 191, A08 ≈ 5, A20 ≈ 2, A01/A04/A06 ≈ 1 each.

After: A27 97.5%, A02 1.0%, A40/A45/A31 0.5% each. Out of 202: A27 ≈ 197, A02 ≈ 2, others 1 each.

I should mention that the share of the dominant transition rose slightly from about 95 in 100 to about 98 in 100, and the set of rare alternative targets changed, but each rare target rests on only 1-5 observations.

Also note: DIR shares are over outgoing transitions, not cases. I'll phrase accordingly.

The inference: insufficient evidence. Limitation: single item, rare transitions with tiny counts, count consistent with chance expectation.

I should not discuss time or resources (no TWAIT/ASSIGN/HAND items). Good.

Format: two sections, concise.
